acc.summary: The schedule as printed on the listing
body: Morning: one tablespoon of the gel. Lunch: one or two Mag Flux capsules. An hour before exercise or sport: one or two Test Drive capsules. The listing names a third occasion which we are not able to reprint on a shop page, because printing it would say what the jar is for.

Always with at least 500 ml of spring water, as printed. The Test Drive sheet prints a different serving again, two capsules with breakfast and at least 1 litre of spring water across the day, and both are set out on the sheet below.
The gel goes in the fridge, used within 28 days of opening or frozen, with a clean dry spoon. Capsules keep their lid on somewhere cool and dry, no fridge.
Not for children. Not in pregnancy or while breastfeeding. The Test Drive listing states that jar is for men only; it gives no reason, and we are not going to invent one.

If you take nitrates, blood pressure medicine, heart medicine or any other prescribed medicine, speak to your GP or pharmacist before you start. Piperine, in Test Drive, is well known to change how the body takes up and clears some medicines. Pine pollen is a pollen, so anyone who reacts to pollen should leave that jar alone. Anyone with an overactive thyroid should leave the sea moss alone, and yellow dock, in Mag Flux, is high in oxalate.

Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. A box with a gel in it goes out chilled. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

spec.label: Kits · 05
spec.intro: Three jars, a price that adds up, and two rows where this listing and the jars in it print different figures.
spec.caption: Men's Health Kit
rows: Contents

One 500 ml jar of the Chondrus Crispus gel. One jar of Mag Flux, 50 large vegan capsules. One jar of Test Drive, 50 large vegan capsules. The listing adds the Konscious Konsumption Nutrition Guide, which it says comes with every order rather than with this box alone.
Price
£99.99. One size, listed with no variants.
Sold separately
£114.97 at the prices on this site: £34.99 plus £39.99 plus £39.99. The box is £14.98 under that. The nutrition guide is not sold separately and carries no price, so it is not in the figure.
Serving

As printed on this listing: one tablespoon of gel each morning, one or two Mag Flux capsules with lunch, one or two Test Drive capsules an hour before exercise or sport, always with at least 500 ml of spring water.
Test Drive, twice

This listing prints one or two capsules before training. The Test Drive listing prints two capsules a day with breakfast, and at least 1 litre of spring water across the day. Both are ours and they do not agree, on the count, the hour or the water. Neither is chosen here.
Volume
This listing prints 500 ml for the gel. The gel's own listing prints no volume at all, and this page does not settle which is right.
Course length
Not printed. No number of days, no number of weeks, and no instruction about stopping.
Storage
Gel: refrigerate, use within 28 days of opening or freeze, clean dry spoon. Capsules: lid on, cool and dry, no fridge.
Suitable for
Adults. No vegan mark on this box: the gel carries Omega DHA oil whose source is not stated on its listing. Both capsule jars carry a vegan mark on their own sheets.
Not printed
No full ingredient list for Mag Flux, which is printed as a proprietary blend. No milligram split for the named plants in Test Drive. No course length for the box.
Not for

Children. Anyone who is pregnant or breastfeeding. Anyone with an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism), because of the seaweed. The Test Drive listing states that jar is for men only and gives no reason for it. If you take nitrates, blood pressure medicine, heart medicine or any other prescribed medicine, speak to your GP or pharmacist before you start. Anyone who reacts to pollen should leave the Test Drive jar alone, and if you have been advised to keep oxalate down, ask first: yellow dock is high in it.
spec.smallprint: Contains iodine from seaweed. Do not exceed the stated dose. Speak to your GP or pharmacist before starting any supplement, particularly if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or take medication. Food supplements should not be used as a substitute for a varied and balanced diet and a healthy lifestyle. Keep out of reach of young children.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The sheet above is three jars, one price, one guide and two rows where our own listings print different numbers for the same jar. Men's Health Kit is the name on the box. It is a name, not a description, and we do not expand it or say what the box is for. What any of these three jars does in a body is not something we are permitted to tell you, so it is not on this page.

reiss.label: Reiss's turn
paras: Test Drive is on this site twice and the two entries do not say the same thing. The jar's own listing prints two capsules with breakfast and a litre of spring water across the day. This box prints one or two an hour before training, with 500 ml. Same jar, same capsules, two different instructions, both written by us. I have put both on the sheet above and picked neither, because picking one quietly would hide the fact that we have been sloppy.

The other thing on that jar is the list of medicines. Nitrates, blood pressure medicine, heart medicine. Piperine as well, which changes how the body takes up and clears some prescriptions. That is not a caution I would bury under a bundle price, so it is in the note at the top of this page and in the last row of the sheet.

The money adds up cleanly for once. The three jars come to £114.97 at the prices on this site, the box is £99.99, so it saves you £14.98. The nutrition guide comes with every order rather than with this box, so it is not in that figure and it is not a reason to buy the box.
reiss.pull: Same jar, same capsules, two different instructions, both written by us.
